Subject: SIG follow-up — clarification on deployment responsibilities

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

Thanks for the SIG spreadsheet you returned yesterday. Our security reviewers flagged a few items where the distinction between Redwood responsibility and customer responsibility isn’t clear across your hosting modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private/VPC). Specifically they asked for: 

- A concise mapping (matrix) that shows who is responsible for: data-at-rest encryption keys, network isolation/segmentation, privileged access (operator/admin access), audit/log generation and retention, and incident response for each mode.
- Any evidence artifacts we can attach to the SIG answers: architecture diagram, SOC 2 attestation, sample audit-log retention policy.
- Confirmation whether Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and whether Private can be deployed air-gapped.

Can you send a one-page matrix + the requested artifacts? Procurement will need a copy of SOC 2 to progress RG approval. If it’s easier we can do a 30‑minute call — availability this week afternoons PST.

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear note. We put together a short ownership matrix and attached artifacts for the SIG review (redwood_infra_mapping_v1.pdf and sig_answer_sheet_filled.xlsx). High-level summary below — full details and evidence are in the PDF.

Quick mapping (responsibility by mode):

Hosted (Redwood API):
- Data-at-rest encryption: Redwood-managed (AES-256); keys managed by Redwood KMS.
- Network isolation: Tenant isolation logical; network controlled by Redwood cloud provider. No dedicated network per customer.
- Privileged access: Redwood operations have limited, logged access; access is role-based and requires approval.
- Audit/logging: Redwood emits request-level logs + platform audit logs; default retention is 1 year.
- Incident response: Redwood PSIRT coordinates for platform incidents; we provide incident notifications and post-incident reports.

Dedicated (Reserved capacity):
- Data-at-rest encryption: Configurable — by default Redwood-managed, and Dedicated supports customer-supplied KMS keys in many deployments (bring-your-own-key flow). See evidence: SOC2 and KMS integration notes in the PDF.
- Network isolation: Dedicated runs in isolated GPU pools with tenant isolation; can be configured inside customer VPC via Private Connect (region dependent).
- Privileged access: Stronger access controls; operator access is limited to the dedicated pool, logged, and can be restricted by RBAC.
- Audit/logging: Customers can request extended retention; we support delivery of audit exports to customer S3/GCS buckets.
- Incident response: Redwood provides playbooks and can integrate with customer on-call rotations under an SLA.

Private (VPC / on-prem):
- Data-at-rest encryption: Customer-managed by default; full BYOK/KMS/HSM patterns supported for on-prem installs.
- Network isolation: Customer-controlled VPC or fully air-gapped on-prem installs.
- Privileged access: Customer retains admin control; Redwood remote support only with explicit allowlists/just-in-time access where needed.
- Audit/logging: Customer controls retention; Redwood agents can forward logs to customer collectors or retain locally per agreement.
- Incident response: Operates under customer SLAs and runbooks; Redwood provides runbook integration and optional managed services.

Evidence we attached:
- redwood_infra_mapping_v1.pdf (2-page matrix + diagrams)
- sig_answer_sheet_filled.xlsx (our completed SIG answers)

Next steps: Please confirm whether the SOC 2 attestation is sufficient for procurement; if you need a notarized copy we'll route that through legal. If acceptable, I can also schedule a deep-dive with Marissa (compliance) to walk the reviewers through the Dedicated/Private KMS options.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the matrix. On a couple of points we need explicit confirmation:

1) SOC 2 — procurement is asking for the most recent SOC 2 Type II reporting period PDF (not just a summary). Can you provide a dated attestation copy?
2) Dedicated KMS — your note says "supports customer-supplied KMS keys in many deployments". Can you clarify: does Dedicated support customer-managed keys in a fully hosted Dedicated model (i.e., Redwood runs the GPUs but the encryption keys never go through Redwood-managed KMS)? If not, does Private (VPC) provide that guarantee?
3) Log retention — we require 3 years of immutable audit logs for our internal compliance. Is that possible via export/archival from Redwood or must that be on Private?

Also cc'ing procurement so they can log the document request (RG approval process). If you can provide SOC2 and a short paragraph for each of the three items above, we can close this section of the SIG.

Thanks,
Marta

Marta — quick answers below and attaching the SOC 2 Type II PDF (SOC2-cert-copy.pdf). Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ABCDEFredwood-sig-evidence (read-only link). HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

1) SOC 2 Type II: attached is the attestation for the latest reporting period (ending 2026-03-31). If you need a signed/notarized physical copy we can route that through legal; that adds ~3–5 business days.

2) Dedicated KMS behavior: Hosted Dedicated (Redwood-managed infrastructure reserved for a customer) can be configured in two ways depending on the procurement path: 
- Standard Dedicated (Redwood-managed KMS): keys are managed by Redwood's KMS, though access to the Dedicated pool is scoped and logged.
- Dedicated with BYOK (bring-your-own-key): in supported regions we can configure Dedicated to use customer-managed keys stored in the customer's cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) via an integration that ensures the key material never persists in Redwood-managed KMS. This pattern requires network connectivity for key authorization (Private Connect or VPC peering) and is included in our Dedicated procurement addendum.

Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-managed keys/HSM support — key material remains under customer control and does not transit Redwood KMS. For air-gapped on-prem installs, all key storage is local to customer hardware.

3) Log retention:
- Hosted: default retention is 12 months; we can export logs to customer storage (S3/GCS) for long-term archival. For immutability/3-year retention we recommend Dedicated with log export or Private deployment where logs are forwarded to a customer-controlled archive. We also support delivery of WORM-style storage to meet immutability requirements, but that requires configuration during onboarding.

Next steps suggested:
- I've attached SOC2-cert-copy.pdf and updated the Drive folder.
- If this satisfies procurement, Marissa and I can sign the SIG with these clarifications and note the required contractual addendum for BYOK on Dedicated.
- I can schedule a 45-minute call tomorrow at 10am PST to walk procurement and security through the integration notes.

Thanks — let me know which next step you prefer.
